title: How does the sum change when both terms change?
description: Starting from one known sum of two negative numbers, three nearby sums are found by following how much each term goes up or down. Keeko's doubt is that minus eighty eight is smaller, so the sum must fall.
teaching_notes: One idea: add up the changes of the two terms to find the change in the sum. Ask the child to say, for each term, whether it went up or down and by how much.

video_script.why: The child sees three new sums found from one known sum by adding up how much each term has changed.
video_script.substitution: Change the numbers and the method stays the same: add the two changes, then change the known sum by that total.
video_script.anchor: the known sum minus 87 plus minus 16 equals minus 103, with a number line below it
video_script.wrong_answer: minus eighty eight is smaller, so the sum must fall
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko looks at only one term, which went down, and forgets that the other term went up by the same amount.
video_script.payoff_line: The first sum is minus one hundred and three.

final_answer.spoken: minus one hundred and three, minus one hundred and four and minus one hundred and twenty three

maths_rules: -88 is 1 less than -87 and -15 is 1 more than -16; the changes -1 and +1 cancel, so -88 + (-15) = -103
-86 is 1 more than -87 and -18 is 2 less than -16; the changes +1 and -2 give -1, so -86 + (-18) = -103 - 1 = -104
-97 is 10 less than -87 and -26 is 10 less than -16; the changes -10 and -10 give -20, so -97 + (-26) = -103 - 20 = -123
video_script.design: One idea: add up the two changes to get the change in the sum. The known sum and the number line stay in the anchor band; the working band shows each change. Keeko's doubt: one term going down makes the sum fall.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>We know that minus eighty seven plus minus sixteen is minus one hundred and three.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>In each new sum, both numbers change a little.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Can we find minus eighty eight plus minus fifteen without adding afresh?

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Each term moves up or down by some amount.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The sum moves by the total of the two changes.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Moves up and moves down can cancel each other.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: −88 + (−15): −88 is 1 less than −87 (−1); −15 is 1 more than −16 (+1); −1 + 1 = 0, so the sum stays −103

marks.m1: −88 is marked one step left of −87, change −1
marks.m2: −15 is marked one step right of −16, change +1
marks.m3: −1 + 1 = 0 is written and the sum stays −103

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, minus eighty eight is one less than minus eighty seven.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Minus fifteen is one more than minus sixteen.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The two changes cancel, so the sum stays the same.

marks.m1: −86 is marked 1 more than −87 and −18 is marked 2 less than −16
marks.m3: −97 is marked 10 less than −87 and −26 is marked 10 less than −16

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, minus eighty six is one more, and minus eighteen is two less.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The changes add up to one less, so the sum is minus one hundred and four.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Minus ninety seven is ten less, and minus twenty six is also ten less.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>The changes add up to twenty less, so the sum is minus one hundred and twenty three.

marks.m3: a tick appears beside each matching value

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, check by adding the two terms.
Eighty eight and fifteen make one hundred and three, so the sum is minus one hundred and three.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Eighty six and eighteen make one hundred and four.
Ninety seven and twenty six make one hundred and twenty three.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>All three match.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>The first sum is minus one hundred and three.
The next is minus one hundred and four, and the last is minus one hundred and twenty three.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Each came from the known sum by adding the two changes.

narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

marks.m3: the arrows −1 and +1 are shown cancelling each other

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Keeko thinks minus eighty eight is smaller, so the sum must fall.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>But minus fifteen is bigger than minus sixteen by the same amount.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The two changes cancel, so both terms must be looked at.
